Subject: Pricing for multi-region pilot

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and the routing controls. We are preparing an internal proposal for a 12-month pilot across three regions (US-West, US-East, EU) and expect steady usage at ~10-15M tokens/month once live.

Given our budget window and the fact this will be a multi-region VPC deployment with some integration work, procurement has asked if Redwood can provide an introductory commercial package with a deeper first-year discount and a VPC setup credit. Rough target from our side is a ~40-45% headline discount vs list for the hosted generation units for months 0-12, plus a setup credit to offset engineering time.

Timeline is tight — procurement needs a commercial term to review by Dec 8 to make the Q1 funding cutoff. Can you confirm whether Redwood will consider a one-time concession for strategic pilot customers, and what the internal approval path looks like? I can loop legal/procurement if helpful.

Attached: Pegasus-SOW-Outline.pdf (high-level scope).

Best,
Arjun

Subject: Re: Pricing for multi-region pilot (internal math)

Laura / Marissa —

I ran the numbers off of Laura’s sketch and Pegasus’s scope. Summary (attached):
- Estimated monthly token consumption (steady-state): 12M tokens
- Targeted headline discount requested by customer: 40-45% for months 1-12
- Net revenue at 45% discount would be below our onboarding + infra cost for a VPC setup and dedicated engineering time.

Proposed internal concession path:
Option A (preferred customer-risk share): 40% discount on hosted generation units for months 0-12, capped at a $150k total consumption credit, and a $100k one-time engineering onboarding credit for VPC setup. Requires VP + CFO signoff.
Option B (reduced ask): 35% discount + $75k onboarding credit; can be approved by VP alone but finance wants a billing safeguard (monthly usage floors or guaranteed minimum).

Operational notes: legal will want the onboarding credit documented as a one-time credit (not rebate), and finance needs a clear billing guardrail to avoid open-ended exposure. I’ve attached a brief deal-summary.xlsx with sensitivity analysis.

Given the strategic nature (multi-region + reference potential), I recommend we escalate for a one-time concession but land closer to Option B to reduce downside. If Marissa agrees, please route to Markus for VP endorsement and loop CFO for final signoff.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
